gloss: family; clan; school (of an art or discipline)

definitions.explanation: A family group or clan sharing a common ancestor or family name. Often used in historical or formal contexts.

definitions.gloss: school; group of disciples (in an art or discipline)
definitions.explanation: A group of practitioners or disciples under one master, especially in traditional arts like sumo, rakugo, tea ceremony, or martial arts.

examples.japanese: {平家|へいけ}{一門|いちもん}が{滅|ほろ}んだ。
{一門|いちもん}の{名誉|めいよ}を{守|まも}る。
examples.english: To protect the honor of the family.

examples.japanese: あの{武将|ぶしょう}は{一門|いちもん}の{長|おさ}として{知|し}られていた。
examples.english: That military commander was known as the head of the clan.

examples.japanese: {師匠|ししょう}の{一門|いちもん}に{入|はい}る。
この{一門|いちもん}には{弟子|でし}が{多|おお}い。
{落語|らくご}の{一門|いちもん}に{入門|にゅうもん}して、{修行|しゅぎょう}を{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: I entered a rakugo school and began my training.

notes:
Refers to a group united by blood ties or by a shared master in a traditional discipline. The word carries a sense of loyalty and shared identity.

SENSE 1 — CLAN/FAMILY:
Common in historical contexts, especially referring to warrior clans of medieval Japan such as {平家|へいけ}{一門|いちもん} (Taira clan) or {源氏|げんじ}{一門|いちもん} (Minamoto clan).

SENSE 2 — SCHOOL/GROUP:
Widely used in traditional arts:
- {相撲|すもう}の{一門|いちもん}: sumo stable group
- {落語|らくご}の{一門|いちもん}: rakugo school
- {茶道|さどう}の{一門|いちもん}: tea ceremony school

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一門|いちもん}に{入|はい}る: to join a school/clan
- {一門|いちもん}の{長|おさ}: head of a clan/school
- {一門|いちもん}を{率|ひき}いる: to lead a clan/school

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {一族|いちぞく}: family, relatives — focuses on blood relations
- {門下|もんか}: disciples under a master — focuses on the student-teacher relationship
- {流派|りゅうは}: school of art — refers to the style or tradition itself
